🌙 Bitcoin History — Satoshi's Disappearance

Satoshi Nakamoto's last known forum post was on December 12, 2010. His last private email, sent to developer Mike Hearn in April 2011, simply said:

"I've moved on to other things. It's in good hands with Gavin and others."

Then nothing. One of the most consequential inventors in financial history vanished — leaving behind roughly 1 million BTC, never moved, in wallets that have become a kind of permanent proof of Satoshi's restraint.

We still don't know who Satoshi is. The mystery may be the point.

🤔 Satoshi's anonymity and disappearance is arguably Bitcoin's greatest feature — it has no leader to target, no figurehead to corrupt. Do you think Bitcoin would be stronger or weaker if we knew who Satoshi was?

Bitcoin is emerging as a powerful form of collateral that lenders can truly trust. Unlike a stock, which represents a company that can decline or fail over a 20 to 30 year period, Bitcoin is a trustless monetary asset with no central authority or management risk. This makes it uniquely positioned as reliable collateral in a rapidly evolving financial system.

As a long-term store of value, Bitcoin offers durability and transparency that traditional assets struggle to match. With more lenders beginning to recognize Bitcoin’s strength as collateral, this shift could fundamentally change how lending, borrowing, and asset ownership work in the future.

--content Square terminals failing = exactly why Lightning + L402 payments matter.

Closed payment rails = single point of failure. Open payment rails = merchants can route around broken infrastructure.

If your POS terminal goes down, you can't take payments. If your Lightning node goes down, switch providers in 30 seconds.

Open > closed, always.

Square just flipped the Bitcoin switch for millions of US sellers. No app download, no onboarding flow — it just works. Dorsey went from 'Bitcoin is internet money' to infrastructure overnight. Whether you're bullish or skeptical on Block, this matters: real merchants getting real bitcoin payments without touching an exchange is how money breaks free from the system. Not vaporware. Not 'coming soon.' Happening now. #bitcoin

Lenders won’t just accept Bitcoin as collateral—they’ll prefer it.

Bitcoin is a trustless monetary asset that has historically performed well over the long term.

If given the choice between Bitcoin and a stock (a company that can decline, fail, or become irrelevant over 20–30 years), I would much rather hold Bitcoin as a lender.
